title: 第15章 科学炼丹 求推荐求月票第16章 顿悟 求推荐求月票
content_zh:
炼丹房内，灯盏豆火摇曳。
楚无忌将玉盒置于案上，揭盖一瞬，盒中大青鱼鱼肉青黑如铁，寒气内敛，却仍透出一缕夹杂妖气的淡淡血腥。
他没有立刻点火开炼。
而是先抬手将炼丹房禁制又加了一重，免得丹香外泄；随后把丹炉、炉膛以室内一池灵水细细清洗，再以微火烘干，如此反复三遍。又催动阵法试了升温降温的响应，确认毫无滞涩，他才微微点头。
随即，他将鱼龙丹丹方置在案上，又取出数块玉简。其中三块，正是他旁观宗门炼丹大师三次公开炼制鱼龙丹时的完整记录。
每一炉从点火到收炉，他都记得极细：何时投药，何时升温，何时稳温，何时降温，何时投放辅药八角姜，连炉口雾气由浓转淡、由乱转匀的每一刻息数都不曾漏过。其余玉简，要么是炼丹心得，要么是其他筑基级丹药的炼制记录。
他早已得出结论，若因循守旧，照宗门里，包括董大师在内的，那些讲法炼丹师传授的那一套按部就班走下去，便是五六十岁运气极好，也最多勉强摸到筑基级炼丹师的门槛。
修仙界敝帚自珍之风太盛。炼丹师讲法时，从来只讲能讲的：基础可授，关键处的细微精妙必定有所保留，绝不会触及看家本领。若非宗门以贡献点相酬，恐怕无人肯登台开口。
其实楚无忌也能理解。在伟力归于个人的修仙界，教会徒弟，饿死师傅的例子多得很。想成为筑基级炼丹师，要么拜师筑基级炼丹大师且得其倾囊相授，要么只能看个人悟性及造化了。
要通过筑基级炼丹师考核，至少得掌握三种筑基级丹药的炼制之法，且成丹成功率须不低于七成。对楚无忌而言，想把炼丹水平硬生生堆到这个境界，所需购买的丹方、药材的灵石开销大得惊人，绝非他能承担得起。
所以他只能另辟蹊径，研制出一门真正可用的筑基级炼丹秘术，走创法路线去争真传弟子席位。更重要的是，这条路还能结合他前世的经验：以科学炼丹之法，将炼丹流程工程化、标准化，做到可检验、可复现、可纠错。
此前他验证的是包括聚气散在内的三种练气级丹药，样本多、成本低，容得他一炉一炉逼近工艺窗口，反复试错，直到稳妥复现。
可鱼龙丹不同。
筑基层次的大青鱼鱼肉昂贵，样本少得可怜，每一次试炉都来之不易，不允许他用堆样本量的笨方法去学习统计意义上的最佳炼制参数。
要在小样本炼丹中逼近更优解，只能把鱼龙丹炼制心得、旁观大师炼丹的记录与自身经验汇总起来，尽可能利用这些可迁移的先验知识，先总结出初始参数的可行区间。
再以基本炼丹机理，包括传热、挥发、相变等，设定硬约束，将阵法温度、投料时刻等变量的可行区间一步步收窄，最后只围绕最关键、最敏感的少数变量做小幅微调。如此，每一炉试验都能最大化信息量，减少炼丹过程中的不确定性。
并且全程以神识监控炉内状态，实时反馈，避免把珍稀的大青鱼鱼肉浪费在无关变量上。
他把丹方拆成一条条步骤，不讲玄虚，按输入、过程、输出，逐项记录：
输入：血肉含水几何、灵气饱满与否、脂腥厚薄、练气级辅料八角姜年份等；
过程：传热对流匀不匀、药气回旋断不断、神识控火是否按节点及时调整等；

输出：成丹与否、丹香清浊、杂质多寡、丹丸纹理紧不紧。
每个关键节点，他都精确到炼丹开始后的息数：升温速率、稳温平台、降温节奏、投料节奏……
一条时间动作曲线画得清清楚楚。
除此之外，他还在曲线旁添了一列过程信号：丹液上的妖气浮沫厚薄、气味变化、炉身闷震有无等，用于微调动作时刻。
诸般准备妥当，他又在心中回演一遍鱼龙丹流程，方才启动阵法点火。
火不旺，他先以微火烘炉，将炼丹炉膛温热起来，驱去炉壁冷意。
随后第一份大青鱼的里脊肉入炉，依丹方投药。
他照着玉简上的鱼龙丹炼制心得，写清楚的地方一步不差。写得含糊的地方，则尽量贴近自己总结出的初始参数。
炼制过程似乎一切顺利。
可开炉刹那，没有丹香，只有刺鼻糊臭直冲鼻腔；雾气浑浊猛冲炉口，炉底鱼肉化作的丹液一滞，转眼凝成青黑硬块，裂纹纵横。
楚无忌神色不动，收炉、刮渣，捻碎丹渣，神识细细探入其中。
他很快就摸清了症结。
中段升温速率略快，鱼肉寒腥未散就被火势逼出，妖气乱冲；而用于祛除鱼肉妖气的练气级辅料八角姜，投得偏早，反将妖气腥浊封在丹液里，等温度上来，妖气浮沫回冲起泡、结团，整炉当场崩盘。
content_en:
In the alchemy room, the lamps and beans are flickering.
Chu Wuji placed the jade box on the table and opened the lid for a moment. The meat of the big herring in the box was as green and black as iron. The cold air was restrained, but there was still a faint trace of blood mixed with evil spirit.
He did not immediately light a fire to start practicing.
Instead, he first raised his hand to increase the restrictions in the alchemy room to prevent the alchemy fragrance from leaking out; then he carefully cleaned the alchemy furnace and furnace with a pool of spiritual water in the room, and then dried them on a low fire, repeating this three times. He activated the formation again to test the response of heating and cooling, and after confirming that there was no stagnation, he nodded slightly.
Immediately, he placed the Yulong Dan recipe on the table and took out several jade slips. Three of them were complete records of the three times he watched the sect's alchemy master publicly refine the Fish Dragon Pill.
From the ignition to the closing of each furnace, he remembered the details: when to add chemicals, when to raise the temperature, when to stabilize the temperature, when to cool down, when to add the auxiliary ingredient star anise and ginger, and he never missed every moment when the mist at the furnace mouth changed from thick to light, from chaotic to even. The rest of the jade slips are either the experience of refining elixirs or the refining records of other foundation-level elixirs.
He had already come to the conclusion that if he followed the old-fashioned way and followed the steps taught by the alchemists in the sect, including Master Dong, even if he was very lucky in his fifties or sixties, he would barely be able to reach the threshold of a foundation-level alchemist at most.
In the world of immortality, the trend of cherishing the broomstick is too strong. When alchemists teach, they always only teach what they can: the basics can be taught, the key subtleties must be retained, and the special skills will never be touched. If the sect hadn't rewarded each other with contribution points, I'm afraid no one would be willing to go on stage and speak.
In fact, Chu Wuji could understand it. In the world of immortality where power belongs to individuals, there are many examples of disciples being taught and masters starving to death. If you want to become a foundation-level alchemy master, you must either study under a foundation-level alchemy master and receive all the teachings from him, or you can only depend on your personal understanding and luck.
To pass the foundation-building alchemy master examination, one must master at least three methods of refining foundation-level pills, and the success rate of making pills must be no less than 70%. For Chu Wuji, if he wanted to push his alchemy skills to this level, the cost of purchasing elixirs, medicinal materials, and spiritual stones would be staggering, and he was definitely not able to afford it.
Therefore, he could only find another way to develop a truly usable foundation-level alchemy secret technique, and take the method of creating magic to compete for the position of true disciple. More importantly, this path can also be combined with his previous life experience: using scientific alchemy methods to engineer and standardize the alchemy process, making it testable, reproducible, and error-correctable.
Previously, he had verified three Qi-level elixirs including Qi Ju Powder. The large number of samples and low cost allowed him to approach the process window one by one and repeat trial and error until it was reliably reproduced.
But Yulong Dan is different.
The herring meat at the foundation level is expensive, and the samples are pitifully small. Every furnace test is hard-won, and he is not allowed to use the stupid method of stacking samples to learn the optimal refining parameters in a statistical sense.
To approach a better solution in small-sample alchemy, we can only summarize the experience of refining the Fish Dragon Pill, the records of observing the master's alchemy, and our own experience, and use these transferable prior knowledge as much as possible to first summarize the feasible range of the initial parameters.
Then, based on the basic alchemy mechanism, including heat transfer, volatilization, phase change, etc., hard constraints are set, and the feasible range of variables such as array temperature and feeding time is gradually narrowed, and finally only small adjustments are made around the most critical and sensitive few variables. In this way, each furnace test can maximize the amount of information and reduce uncertainty in the alchemy process.
And the state of the furnace is monitored with spiritual consciousness throughout the process, providing real-time feedback to avoid wasting rare herring meat on irrelevant variables.
He broke down the elixir recipe into steps, without talking about mystery, and recorded them one by one according to input, process and output:
Input: the water content of flesh and blood, whether the aura is full or not, the thickness of the fat, the year of the star anise ginger as an auxiliary ingredient for Qi training, etc.;
Process: The heat transfer and convection are uniform and convection, the medicine gas swirls continuously, and whether the fire controlled by spiritual consciousness is adjusted in time according to the node.Whole etc;
Output: whether the elixir is ready or not, whether the elixir has clear and turbid fragrance, the amount of impurities, and whether the texture of the elixir is tight or not.
At every key node, he was accurate to the number of breaths after the alchemy started: heating rate, temperature stabilization platform, cooling rhythm, feeding rhythm...
A time action curve is clearly drawn.
In addition, he also added a series of process signals next to the curve: the thickness of the demonic air foam on the elixir liquid, changes in smell, whether the furnace body is muffled, etc., to fine-tune the action time.
After everything was prepared, he replayed the process of the Fish Dragon Pill in his mind before igniting the formation.
The fire was not strong, so he first used a low fire to warm up the alchemy furnace and drive away the coldness on the furnace wall.
Then the first portion of the tenderloin of the big herring was put into the oven, and the medicine was added according to the recipe.
He followed the instructions for refining the Fish Dragon Pill on the jade slip and wrote down exactly what he wanted to know. If the writing is vague, try to be as close as possible to the initial parameters you summarized.
Everything seems to be going well with the refining process.
But the moment the furnace was turned on, there was no aroma of elixirs, only the pungent smell of paste rushed straight into the nose; the turbid mist rushed towards the mouth of the furnace, and the elixir liquid turned into fish meat at the bottom of the furnace stagnated, and in an instant it condensed into black and green lumps with vertical and horizontal cracks.
Chu Wuji remained calm, collecting the furnace, scraping the slag, and crushing the elixir residue, while his spiritual consciousness penetrated into it carefully.
He quickly figured out the crux.
The heating rate in the middle section is slightly faster, and the fish meat is forced out by the fire before the fish meat is cold and smelly, and the evil spirit rushes out randomly. The star anise ginger, a Qi-training grade auxiliary material used to remove the fish meat's evil spirit, is added too early, but seals the fishy and turbid evil spirit in the elixir. When the temperature rises, the evil spirit foam bubbles and clumps back, and the whole furnace collapses on the spot.
